issues.legal_issue: An award based on agricultural yield is not invalid merely because it omits a deduction for cultivation expenses when the acquired land includes productive fruit-bearing trees.
material_facts: Some of the acquired land had cashew-nut trees that were sufficiently old and productive, and other portions were used for crops.
The acquiring authority argued that cultivation expenses should have been deducted from the yield-based valuation.
The court distinguished the cited case involving ordinary crop cultivation, where it had treated average cultivation expenses as a substantial share of crop value.
issues.conclusion: On these facts, the absence of a deduction for cultivation expenses did not make the enhanced award illegal.
issues.legal_principle: In State of Gujarat v. Rama Rana, (1987) 2 SCC 693, the Court held that cultivation expenses must be considered when land is valued on yield and that, in the circumstances of that case, a one-third deduction was insufficient. That approach does not strictly apply to fruit-growing trees, for which expenses would not be 50% as in ordinary crop cultivation. The applicable inquiry is whether the deduction is justified by the evidence and the kind of cultivation shown.

predicates.land_acquisition_compensation_appeal: An acquiring authority appeals a determination of compensation for land taken through compulsory acquisition.
predicates.yield_based_valuation: The compensation determination relies on the income or produce of the acquired land.
predicates.productive_fruit_trees_evidenced: Evidence shows that the acquired land included sufficiently mature fruit-bearing trees.

issues.definition: When an acquiring authority appeals a yield-based compensation determination and evidence shows productive fruit-bearing trees on the land, omission of a cultivation-expense deduction does not by itself invalidate the award.

issues.legal_issue: Valuation of acquired land by capitalization of yield requires use of the appropriate standard multiplier rather than an excessive multiplier.
material_facts: The Reference Court used a multiplier of 20 years when capitalizing the land's income.
The Supreme Court considered the established decisions addressing capitalization of agricultural yield.
The Supreme Court found the multiplier used by the Reference Court to be excessive, while ultimately assessing the compensation in light of other circumstances as well.
issues.conclusion: A multiplier of 20 was contrary to the settled approach; the appropriate multiplier for yield-based capitalization is 10.
issues.legal_principle: Special Land Acquisition, Davangere v. P. Veerabhadarappa, (1984) 2 SCC 120; Special Land Acquisition Officer v. Virupax Shankar Nadagouda, (1996) 6 SCC 124; Krishi Utpadan Mandi Samiti v. Malik Sartaj Wali Khan, (2001) 10 SCC 660; and Assistant Commissioner-cum-Land Acquisition Officer, Bellary v. S.T. Pompanna Setty, (2005) 9 SCC 662, establish that a multiplier of 10 is proper when compensation is computed on yield. Special Land Acquisition Officer, Bangalore v. T. Adinarayan Setty, (1959) Supp (1) SCR 404, and Smt. Tribeni Devi v. Collector of Ranchi, (1972) 1 SCC 480, explain that market value may be assessed using recognized valuation methods, including capitalization of profits, while taking relevant circumstances into account to reach the nearest correct market value.

predicates.land_acquisition_compensation_appeal: An acquiring authority appeals a determination of compensation for land taken through compulsory acquisition.
predicates.yield_based_capitalization: The compensation is calculated by capitalizing the income or yield of the acquired land.

issues.definition: When an acquiring authority appeals a compensation determination calculated by capitalizing yield, the calculation uses the appropriate standard multiplier.

issues.legal_issue: Enhanced compensation may be upheld when comparable transactions, awards for similar nearby land, and the land's potentiality support the valuation, even if the lower court used an excessive capitalization multiplier or the appellate court gave inadequate reasons.
material_facts: A sale transaction showed a price of Rs. 19,800 per acre for land in a nearby village.

Reference Court awards for land acquired for the same purpose in nearby or the same village set compensation at Rs. 22,000 per acre, and the High Court had dismissed an appeal concerning one such award.
The acquiring authority had itself awarded Rs. 12,000 per acre for other land in the same village.
The land had crop and cashew-nut cultivation, and the Reference Court's finding that there were no cashew trees was factually incorrect.

The High Court awarded Rs. 22,000 per acre, although it did not give adequate reasons; the Supreme Court considered the valuation and the land's potentiality and utility and found the award adequate and reasonable.
issues.conclusion: The enhanced compensation of Rs. 22,000 per acre was upheld and the appeals were dismissed.
issues.legal_principle: Under Section 4(1) of the Land Acquisition Act, 1894, market value is assessed as of the notification date. T. Adinarayan Setty identifies expert opinion, bona fide comparable transactions, and capitalization of actual or immediately prospective profits as valuation methods; Tribeni Devi permits consideration of other circumstances to reach the nearest correct market value. The Court may consider land potentiality and utility alongside yield valuation. The principles in P. Veerabhadarappa and the later multiplier cases establish the appropriate multiplier for yield-based valuation, but an excessive multiplier does not require disturbing an award otherwise supported by comparable evidence and the circumstances of the land.

rule.if: land_acquisition_compensation_appeal and comparable_transaction_evidence and comparable_award_evidence and land_potentiality_supported

predicates.land_acquisition_compensation_appeal: An acquiring authority appeals an enhanced determination of compensation for land taken through compulsory acquisition.
predicates.comparable_transaction_evidence: Evidence shows bona fide transactions for land with similar advantages in the relevant area.
predicates.comparable_award_evidence: Awards for nearby or otherwise similar land acquired for a comparable purpose support the valuation.
predicates.land_potentiality_supported: Evidence about the land's use, productivity, or utility supports the assessed market value.

issues.definition: When an acquiring authority appeals enhanced compensation and comparable transactions, comparable awards, and the land's potentiality support the valuation, the enhanced compensation is upheld.
